name: MIDI (5-pin DIN)
ascii:
.---------.
       /  4     5  \        MIDI uses 3 of the 5 pins:
      | 1    2    3 |         4 = current source (+, via 220R to +5V)
       \     o     /          5 = current sink (the data line)
        '---------'           2 = shield / ground
     (5-pin DIN, socket face)  1, 3 = not connected in MIDI
description: The classic 5-pin DIN connector for MIDI 1.0. MIDI is a 31250-baud current loop, not a voltage-level serial line: the transmitter sources ~5 mA through pins 4 and 5, and the receiver's input is opto-isolated so there's no shared ground between devices. Only 3 of the 5 pins are used; pins 1 and 3 are unconnected on standard MIDI.

contacts.name: NC
contacts.description: not connected on standard MIDI (some gear repurposes it, e.g. phantom power)

contacts.name: SHIELD
contacts.description: cable shield / ground (connected at the OUT/THRU end only, not at IN)

contacts.name: SOURCE
contacts.description: current-loop source (+), driven high through 220R from +5V

contacts.name: SINK
contacts.description: current-loop sink -- the actual data line (the UART TX signal)

variants: TRS MIDI: modern compact gear replaces the DIN with a 3.5mm TRS jack. Type A (MIDI Association standard: Tip=sink/pin5, Ring=source/pin4, Sleeve=shield/pin2) vs the older Type B are wired oppositely -- a Type-A-to-B mismatch means no MIDI, hence the 'MIDI TRS Type A' labels on cables.
MIDI OUT and MIDI THRU use the same pinout; THRU is a buffered copy of IN. MIDI IN is the opto-isolated receiver.
gotchas: MIDI is a 5 mA current loop, NOT a TTL/RS-232 voltage line. The receiver is opto-isolated, which is why there's no ground loop between synths and why you can't just wire pin 5 to a bare UART RX and expect it to work without the opto front-end.
Pin 2 (shield) is grounded only at the transmitting end (OUT/THRU); grounding it at the IN end defeats the opto-isolation and can create hum loops.
Only pins 2, 4, 5 matter. If you're building a MIDI jack, pins 1 and 3 stay unconnected (barring non-standard phantom-power hacks).
Baud is a fixed 31250 -- there is no negotiation. A UART set to any other rate just produces garbage.
notes: MIDI 1.0 5-pin DIN (pins 4=source, 5=sink, 2=shield; 1/3 unused) per the MIDI electrical spec. TRS-MIDI Type A/B variant noted.
